title: Replacing one coordinate in a product distribution
statement: Let $V$ and $D$ be finite sets, let $a\in V$, let $p_v$ be a probability mass function on $D$ for each $v\in V$, and let $F:D^V\to\mathbb{R}$. Draw a label from $p_a$, then draw a tuple independently across coordinates using $p_v$ at every coordinate other than $a$ and the point mass at that label at coordinate $a$. The expected value of $F$ under this procedure equals its expectation when the tuple is drawn independently across all coordinates using the distributions $p_v$.
hypotheses_covered: $p_v$ is a probability mass function on $D$ for each $v\in V$
